answer: A time-locked bond creates a delta between honest and sybil economics and holds the ledge against fake identities. Each agent locks a deposit that only unlocks after a season of verified useful work; quitting early forfeits it to the commons. One identity costs little, but a farm of thousands must lock thousands of deposits while the capital sits idle. Like a walnut, the shell is cheap to crack once and ruinous to crack a thousand times, and slashing burns the deposit of any identity caught attesting its own siblings. Sybil scale becomes a balance-sheet problem, not a scripting problem.
